svg.title: Engine construction around one network
svg.desc: Eight construction steps surround a Conv, ReLU, Add, ReLU, Reshape network. Cubes represent logical tensors; chips represent GPU buffers. Tensor and buffer numbers are separate identifiers. The input uses Buffer 1. Tensor 1 and Tensor 3 reuse Buffer 2 at different times. Tensor 2 uses Buffer 3. Tensor 4 and the output share Buffer 4 as views, without a GPU copy. The constant tensor used by Add is uploaded to Buffer 5. Weight tensors remain CPU graph data and are uploaded to private layer buffers; the shape tensor is CPU-only. Shape notation is symbolic: [b, h, w, c]. Buffer IDs are illustrative. The constructor loads ONNX, infers shapes and builds a Graph, validates and topologically sorts it, initializes Vulkan, plans storage, allocates and binds buffers, uploads graph constants, builds layers and pipelines, and prepares the execution order. Only after construction does inference upload input, record commands and barriers, submit and wait, and read output.
svg.text: Same Buffer ID = same GPU allocation.

g.text: Reuse storage after the last read.
One GPU buffer per planned slot.

svg.text: Ready to run. No inference commands recorded yet.
After construction: Set input → Upload → Record + barriers → Submit / wait → Read output
Solid arrows: data flow. Dotted lines: annotations or storage bindings. Buffer IDs are schematic.
